University of Science and Technology of China (Wang, Zhang, Mao); 'Independent researchers' (Sun, Zhu, Zhou, Liu, Chen, Qiu, Cao, Cai). Seed queries sampled from 'a production web development service' and 'our production user traffic', organisation not named

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — Asuka-Bench benchmark (underspecified web-development requests resolved in a closed loop: Code Agent builds, UI Agent tests in the browser, User LLM gives feedback); 8 LLMs across 2 agent frameworks compared; one-shot Clarified PRD vs three rounds on the underspecified query compared (RQ1)

No SDD approach. Agent frameworks OpenHands and Claude Code ('our in-house Claude Code sandbox'), versions not stated. Backbone models: GPT-5.4 (Medium), Gemini-3.1-Pro, Claude-4.6-Sonnet, GLM-5, Kimi-K2.6, Seed-2.0-Pro, MiniMax-M2.7, Qwen3.5-Plus; Table 1 also lists LongCat-Preview and LongCat-2.0-Preview on Claude Code. Conditions: underspecified query with up to 3 feedback rounds vs single round on the Clarified PRD (PRD-1R). Evaluator: GPT-5.4 as UI Agent (BrowserUse-based) and User LLM

Agent receives only an underspecified natural-language query (body at most 200 words, derived from the PRD). Hidden ground truth: Clarified PRD (structured requirements document: overview, functional modules, fault tolerance and exception handling, appearance), evaluation criteria (Presence / Functionality / Robustness tasks with difficulty weight 1-5 and prerequisite DAG, each with expected outcomes), simulated data; per-round natural-language feedback from the User LLM. In PRD-1R the agent receives the Clarified PRD

Closed loop per task: (1) Code Agent generates the web project from the query; (2) project deployed, UI Agent executes criteria as browser test cases in DAG topological order (skip tasks with failed prerequisites, soft threshold T=0.5); (3) User LLM turns failed results into feedback; (4) Code Agent refines; repeat until all pass or 3 rounds (8 in the saturation analysis)
None in the loop: the user is simulated by an LLM. Humans only annotate final-round projects for evaluator validation
Full workflow of each agent (generation and feedback-driven repair); the specification given to the agent is varied (underspecified query vs Clarified PRD) in RQ1
Not classifiable; authors' wording: 'Clarified PRD (Product Requirements Document), a structured specification', 'underspecified user intent', 'a full spec'
New project: self-contained web frontends generated from scratch with simulated data (no backend)

50 tasks; 784 evaluation tasks (Presence 129, Functionality 492, Robustness 163) with 2,402 expected outcomes; 15.7 evaluation tasks per PRD, 3.1 expected outcomes per task, mean difficulty weight 2.96, mean DAG depth 4.4 (max 9). Project code size Not stated

Web front-end applications in six categories (ArtifactsBench taxonomy): Utility 38%, Data Visualization 22%, Management System 20%, E-Commerce 8%, Marketing/Display 6%, Social 6%; queries from online user data, GitHub repositories and existing websites

Automatic: GPT-5.4 vision-enabled UI Agent in headless Chrome (BrowserUse-based) executes each criterion on the deployed site (max 100 steps per criterion, 3600 s timeout, max 3 retries per DAG layer, concurrency 3) and returns Pass/Fail with explanation; metrics computed from per-criterion results; 95% CIs by CLT over 50 per-project values. Manual: single human annotator per criterion on 50 sampled Round-3 projects (3,576 annotations) with a written rubric and console. Criteria and PRDs generated by an LLM (model not named)

Tasks: 50 Asuka-Bench web tasks. Configurations: model x framework (OpenHands, Claude Code); stated as 13, Table 1 lists 15; three cells skipped (Gemini and Kimi on Claude Code: protocol not supported; Sonnet on OpenHands: budget). Baseline: single-round Clarified PRD (PRD-1R) for six Claude Code models; Flat evaluation protocol as baseline for the DAG protocol. Held constant: queries, evaluator and User LLM (GPT-5.4), max 3 rounds, DAG threshold T=0.5, default model temperature. Acceptance tests: natural-language criteria executed by the UI Agent. Repetitions: 1 run per task per cell (50 projects treated as i.i.d.). Human intervention: none (simulated user)

Best: GPT-5.4 on OpenHands (R3 90.1%, PCR 52%) and Claude-4.6-Sonnet on Claude Code (89.4%, PCR 46%); worst Seed-2.0-Pro (51.8-53.7%); 38-pp range with non-overlapping 95% CIs at the top and bottom only (no formal tests). Round 2 adds about 25 pp, Round 3 7-13 pp. RQ1: first ambiguous round is 9-18 pp below PRD-1R, but every model exceeds its PRD-1R score by Round 3 (net +8.7 to +26.6 pp); rankings shift between protocols. RQ2: repair ability decoupled from first-round quality (Kimi-K2.6 on OpenHands 44.3 -> 74.7 -> 86.6). Frameworks (5 shared models): OpenHands higher PCR (29.2% vs 25.6%), Task Pass Rate tied (72.5% vs 72.6%); Claude Code about 1.8x faster (64.5 vs 116.3 min/project). DAG vs Flat: DAG cuts evaluation tokens 23-26% (GLM-5 17.9M vs 23.4M) with higher fix rates, slightly lower pass rates

Distinguished configurations (38-pp range, CIs non-overlapping at extremes) and showed a repair-from-feedback axis. Not repeated (1 run per task); CIs over projects only. Evaluator validated against single-annotator human labels (93.35% accuracy). Limitations stated: evaluator dependence on GPT-5.4 (swapping it may shift absolute scores), single-annotator gold labels, CLT normal approximation can degrade near 0/1 for PCR, cross-row fix-rate comparisons depend on different denominators, Flat numbers taken from a previous version of the work

Limitations: domain coverage (50 tasks, six categories, self-contained frontends with simulated data; 3D, real-time collaborative and live-backend scenarios out of scope); evaluator dependence on GPT-5.4 and single-annotator validation; possible contamination of queries and DAGs by future training (needs periodic refresh). Gaps: static one-shot benchmarks miss iterative refinement and repair-from-feedback ability
